name: Lanternfish Tiling Conjecture
summary: Made-up sample problem. A lanternfish tile is a fictional seven-sided shape with one curved edge. The conjecture says that lanternfish tiles can cover the infinite plane, with no gaps or overlaps, only in patterns that never repeat. Small patches have been checked by computer and a promising proof strategy exists, but no complete proof or counterexample has been accepted.

progress.title: Problem posed and the tile defined precisely
progress.description: The tile's angles and edge lengths were fixed, and the question was stated in its current form.

progress.title: Computer search finds no repeating patch up to 10,000 tiles
progress.description: An exhaustive search found no periodic patch of up to 10,000 tiles, which is evidence for the conjecture but not a proof.

progress.title: Substitution-rule proof attempt
progress.description: A proof using a simple inflation rule failed because the curved edge cannot be split evenly. Do not retry this route without a new way to handle the curved edge.

links.title: Write-up of the failed attempt (sample link)

progress.title: Edge-marking argument rules out every periodic tiling
progress.description: A new marking of the curved edge may force aperiodicity. The draft is being checked line by line.

progress.title: Machine-checked formal proof
progress.description: Formalise the complete argument in a proof assistant so the result does not rest on a hand check.
